tasks.short: Restock supplies, rotate food and date food in coolers

steps.what: Restock kitchen supplies in their correct storage locations
Rotate food according to date and condition
Stamp the correct time and date on food in coolers

tasks.design: Retain physical restocking, rotation and date stamping. Existing storage guidance in {DOCS} supports the work; a pre-existing date stamp already simplifies marking and earns no new saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Food must be moved, inspected and labelled physically.
tasks.enabler_now: No supported change removes those actions.
tasks.still_hard: Correct dates and actual food condition need checks.
tasks.human_edge: The cook notices damaged packaging, deterioration or ambiguous labels.
tasks.altitude: No change in physical work or food-safety responsibility.

evidence.claim: Food movement, rotation and date stamping remain physical work in this scenario.

assumptions: Boundary covers restocking, rotation and labelling, excluding purchasing and cooking.
Cook verifies food identity and actual preparation or storage time within retained steps; no free structured expiry or safety flag is assumed.
The shelving action is the same as task2194 s3. Roll-up owner is task18725; count common shelving once. No new technology or upkeep is introduced, justifying zero incremental work.
research_questions: Which storage problems require physical checks despite existing labels?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100, zero upkeep; existing stamping is baseline and all physical work remains.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan orders so jointly served items finish together

steps.what: Read orders and assess cooking times and current station capacity
Plan preparation sequences and coordinate items to finish at the same time

tasks.design: Keep live order sequencing with the cook. Existing order displays in {OTHER}, the kitchen order system where present, support the task but do not replace checking actual station progress.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cooking duration varies with load and real food condition.
tasks.enabler_now: The digest supplies no validated short-order sequencing change.
tasks.still_hard: Late modifications and uneven station progress.
tasks.human_edge: The cook adjusts timing from direct observation.
tasks.altitude: No change to sequencing time or decisions.

reach.learn: Clear timing calls and progress checks

evidence.claim: Live cooking coordination remains human work in this scenario.

assumptions: Boundary is cook planning and coordination, excluding actual food preparation counted in task2190.
Cook determines timing and observes progress within s1 and s2. No structured ready-time or station-capacity feed is assumed.
Existing tickets or displays remain baseline tools. No new upkeep is introduced, justifying zero incremental work.
research_questions: Which timing decisions depend on live food and station observations?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100, zero upkeep; no live planning or coordination time is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Take customer orders and cook short-preparation foods

steps.what: Take orders from customers and clarify their food requirements
Prepare and cook foods to the confirmed customer requirements

tasks.design: Retain customer clarification and physical cooking. Existing order records in {OTHER}, the kitchen order system where present, support communication without eliminating the cook's interaction or food handling.
tasks.previous_blocker: Customer requirements and food condition require real-time attention.
tasks.enabler_now: No supported change removes cooking or clarification.
tasks.still_hard: Special requirements and changing cooking conditions.
tasks.human_edge: The cook confirms requests and judges food readiness.
tasks.altitude: No change in cooking and customer-contact time.

evidence.claim: Customer clarification and cooking remain human work in this scenario.

assumptions: Boundary is taking the order and cooking, excluding payment and separate sequencing work in task2188.
Cook elicits food choices and special requirements in s1's25 hours. No structured allergen or availability flag is assumed; uncertain requests are clarified manually.
No new system or upkeep is introduced, justifying zero incremental work.
unknowns: Customer request mix and order process
research_questions: Which requests need direct clarification before cooking?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 and zero upkeep; no customer interaction or cooking effort is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Order supplies and stock them on shelves

steps.what: Check stock and determine the supplies and quantities needed
Prepare, check and submit orders for needed supplies
Restock kitchen supplies in their correct shelf and storage locations

tasks.design: Configure reusable supply lists in {PROCUREMENT} after checking stock physically. The cook adjusts quantities, checks the complete order before submission and still shelves all received supplies.
tasks.previous_blocker: Recurring supply items may be entered repeatedly in supplier orders.
tasks.enabler_now: Native saved baskets and order forms can reuse selected item details.
tasks.still_hard: Actual stock, substitutions and kitchen demand need checking.
tasks.human_edge: The cook chooses sensible quantities from real stock and requirements.
tasks.altitude: Less order entry; purchasing and physical stocking responsibilities remain.

evidence.claim: Native recurring order lists can reduce entry time; no measured short-order cook saving is supplied.

assumptions: Boundary covers requirements, ordering and shelving, excluding supplier fulfilment. The common shelving action belongs to task18725 in team roll-ups and must not be counted twice.

Cook produces item identity, observed usable quantity and required order quantity in s1's20 hours. Supplier maintains existing catalogue item, unit and price through unchanged catalogue work. Cook verifies missing details and substitutions within s2's15 remaining hours; no free par level or stock feed is assumed.
Test native saved lists first. Physical stock checking and shelving retain their full shares.
research_questions: Do saved lists reduce ordering after stock checks and substitutions?

incremental.description: Maintain reusable supply lists and resolve order exceptions

approvals.approved_version: Exact final supplier, items, quantities, units, costs and delivery details; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R85 gives15 gross minus3 upkeep net12. Low assumes only3 hours repeat entry removed; stock checks20 and shelving50 remain full. Shared shelving is counted once at roll-up.

role.altitude: Less repeated supply ordering, with food handling, live timing and customer clarification unchanged.
reach: Coordinate accurate orders with counter workers
